title: Ah! Carry My Heart to Heaven!
text:
How I Adore You!


Oh, how I adore you! With the light of day

I invoke your name, impassioned and

sad,

and when the sky dresses itself in shadows,

my exalted soul still calls to you.

You

are the time that guides my hours,

you are the idea that attends my mind,

because in you is found all that exists,

my passion, my

hope, my poetry.

There is

no song that can equal your accent

when, my love, you tell me and

rave,

revealing the faith of your contentment;


I tremble at your voice and tremble if you look at me,

and I would like to exhale my last

breath

burning in the air you breathe.
editorial_note: This catalog-title variant preserves the embedded How I Adore You heading and the source's slightly different phrasing.

title: The Moon Is an Absence
text:
And you, who are you, wandering night's

apparition passing silently,

crossing the undulating spaces

behind the vapors of the watery cloud?


Black the earth, sad the firmament,

blind my eyes were without your light,

and sighing in the dark wind

shadowy spirits wandered.


I awaited you, and when I saw your red

outlines appear with slow calm,

as your ray descended to my eyes,

tender joy descended to my soul.


And do you come lazily to my prayers

when the loving heart longs for you?

Come to me, soft light, nocturnal, beautiful

daughter of heaven, come: why so late!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Coronado's apostrophe to the moon as a delayed heavenly presence.

title: Each Word a Leaf
text:
Each word a leaf

In the right place.


A flower now and then

On the open branch.


A bird seemed

Standing and near.


But no: for the verse went and came

Through the universe.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Meireles's compact craft image: word, leaf, flower, bird, and verse moving through the universe.

title: Light Is the Bird...
text:
Light is the bird:

And its flying shadow,

Lighter.


And the airy waterfall,

From its throat,

Lighter.


And what remembers, hearing

Its song slide by,

Lighter.


And the swift desire

Of this ancient instant,

Lighter.


And the invisible flight

Of the bitter passerby,

Lighter.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the repeated comparative lightness that moves from bird to shadow, song, memory, desire, and vanishing.

title: Since the Comrade Is Dead...
text:
Since the comrade is dead,

All of us together die

a little.


The value of our tears

Over the one who lost his life

is nothing.


Love, in this sadness,

Is a sigh in a forest,

Is a good idea.


Out of straight fidelity

To the lost comrade,

What remains to us?


To let ourselves die a little

For the one whom today we see

Wholly dead.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the restrained communal mourning and fidelity to the dead comrade.
